PullRequest.Title: Load multi-diff text models and compute diffs on demand
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #240181

Opening the multi-file diff editor for a large change set (for example a commit with thousands of files) used to load the text models of both sides of every file and start a diff computation for each of them before anything was shown. With many files this keeps Git and the renderer busy for minutes, and the editor stays at "Loading..." the whole time.

With this change, the editor only loads what is shown:

- The file list is published immediately, without reading any contents. Each entry carries a `resolve` function that loads its text models on demand.
- Only the first 5 files are loaded and diffed up front, so the first diffs appear quickly.
- Other files load when they become visible and expanded, or when navigation targets them (reveal, next/previous change, restored view state). Collapsed files are never loaded.
- Navigation, focus, and selection restoration wait until the target file's diff is ready.
- A file that fails to load stays in the list and shows "Unable to load this file."; its error is reported once. Previously such files were dropped from the editor, which required loading every file first.
- Save and revert handle dirty files of entries that were never loaded, without loading them.
- Loaded models are kept until the editor is disposed; there is no eviction yet.

## Demo

400 changed files opened with **Git: Open Changes**, first in current VS Code Insiders, then in a build with this change. The captions show how many files Git was asked to read, counted from the Git output log.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Files read when the diff appears | 400 of 400 (editor shows "Loading..." until done) | 5 |
| After jumping to the middle of the list | 400 | 11 |

**Before** (current VS Code Insiders):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d2daf6f-97d2-492c-aa35-90c2725d9069

**After** (this change):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8db0129a-eaae-4dd6-ab70-3c1cb6ab9750

Dragging the scrollbar slowly through the list still loads every file that becomes visible on the way.

## Implementation notes

- `IDocumentDiffItem` gets an optional `resolve` function. `MultiDiffEditorInput` creates lightweight entries and resolves text models in `_resolveDocument`; failures are reported per item instead of dropping the item.
- `DocumentDiffItemViewModel` now creates its `DiffEditorViewModel` lazily in `load()` and exposes `isLoaded` and `loadError`. `MultiDiffEditorViewModel.waitForDiffOr1s` waits only for the first 5 items.
- `DiffEditorItemTemplate` shows a "Loading..." placeholder (with `aria-busy`) until the item is loaded, then attaches the diff model.
- The resource ordering added to `MultiDiffEditorInput` in #344716 now orders the lightweight entries, so reordering does not load contents.

## How to test

1. Create a repository with a few hundred modified files.
2. Run **Git: Open Changes**: the first diffs appear quickly and the Git output shows `git show` calls only for the first few files.
3. Scroll or jump far down: only the newly visible files are read.
4. Use next/previous change and collapse/expand files across unloaded entries.

## Validation

- Unit tests for `multiDiffEditorInput`, `multiDiffEditorWidget`, `multiDiffEditorWithFileList`, `sessionChangesEditor` and `textModelResolverService`, run with both `node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --run <file>…` (73 passing) and `scripts\test.bat --run <file>…` in Electron (74 passing). New tests cover the 5-item limit with 1,000 entries, on-demand loading, slow and failing loads (reported once), removal while loading, saving unloaded dirty files, collapsed files staying unloaded, and deferred reveal, next-change, focus, and view-state restoration. Existing tests whose mocks lacked `IEditorProgressService.show` now provide it, because diffs can now be attached before they finish computing.
- Type check of `src/tsconfig.json` (as in `pnpm run typecheck-client`): passed.
- Commit hygiene (formatting, copyright) passed via the pre-commit hook.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Opening a multi-diff with N files eagerly acquired up to 2N text-model references and started N diff computations before the model could be published, placing filesystem/content-provider/Git reads and diff CPU for the entire change set on the editor-open critical path.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Large SCM/history change sets could leave the multi-diff editor loading while all file contents were resolved and all diffs were started; the cost and external reads scaled linearly with total files rather than the visible initial batch.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The editor now publishes all lightweight file entries immediately, resolves text models only through each entry's on-demand resolve callback, and starts only the first five diffs initially; visible/navigation-targeted items reuse a per-item ObservableLazyPromise, so each requested file resolves once.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, line 218 constructs an async mapped entry for every resource; that mapper calls createModelReference for both sides, and _createModel awaits Promise.all of the entire mapped collection before publishing documents. MultiDiffEditorViewModel then creates a DiffEditorViewModel and waits for each item's initial diff. The changed code instead publishes URI-only entries whose added resolve callback is invoked lazily, while MultiDiffEditorViewModel limits startup loading to items.slice(0, 5). The added 1,000-entry test asserts exactly 10 model-reference requests and 5 diff computations at initial open, directly establishing the reduced cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a large SCM group, commit/history item, session change set, or pull-request change set in the multi-diff editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The source resolver must first publish file metadata. The changed model then publishes URI-only entries immediately and waits for at most the first five item loads/diffs (with the input's one-second race) before the editor can progress; all other content work is off the initial critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the change-set metadata through the SCM/history provider or GitHub service before constructing MultiDiffEditorItem entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical source-resolution request per editor open, returning N file descriptors; provider internals may perform network, extension-host, or Git work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same source resolution was required before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Metadata resolution remains required before the file list is available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire original and modified text-model references, which resolves file/content-provider data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold open resolves up to two sides for each of the first five files: at most 10 concurrent acquisitions for a two-sided initial batch. One-sided additions/deletions issue fewer. Cached model references can make acquisitions warm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base code eagerly acquired up to 2N model references and awaited Promise.all for every file before publishing the model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the initial five loads are awaited, subject to the editor input's one-second outer race; remaining files do not block opening.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute document diffs in the editor worker after each pair of text models resolves.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most five initial diff computations, launched concurrently after their corresponding model loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base path constructed a diff view model for every resolved file and started N diff computations before initial readiness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial presentation waits for those five computations or their one-second limits; the input itself also has a one-second race.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total changed files N; the changed boundary cost on cold open is capped to min(N, 5) files rather than N, while O(N) lightweight URI/view-model entries remain.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The first five items load in parallel; each item acquires its original and modified model in parallel, yielding at most 10 model acquisitions and five diff computations for a two-sided initial batch. There is no global limiter, but the fixed batch bounds the startup burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each item uses one ObservableLazyPromise, coalescing concurrent load callers and caching success or failure. Loaded text/diff models remain retained until the item/editor is disposed. Text-model resolver references may also hit its shared collection on warm loads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the old all-resource Promise.all path, new five-item slice, two model-reference calls per two-sided item, and one diff per loaded item are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency and file size vary, but the before/after cardinality is directly established by the code and the added 1,000-item test.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. This is a substantial eager-work and boundary-fanout reduction; the concrete pre-existing regression fix was recorded separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll through, expand, reveal, restore, focus, or navigate to an initially unloaded file
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A rendered expanded item or explicit navigation calls the item's coalesced load, resolves its text models, starts one diff, and navigation waits for that diff before positioning/focusing. Unrelated offscreen or collapsed items remain off the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve both sides of a newly visible/targeted file through MultiDiffEditorInput._resolveDocument.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two acquisitions per newly encountered unique file; repeated visibility or multiple simultaneous callers reuse the same promise. Effective multiplicity is the number of unique expanded files entering the virtualized viewport or explicit navigation targets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, every file had already been resolved during editor open, so scrolling itself did not initiate this boundary; however the user could not reach scrolling until all N files had loaded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: First access shows a loading placeholder or waits before range/change navigation; warm access is immediate from the cached loaded item.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute and await the target file's diff in the editor worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One computation per newly loaded unique file; repeated navigation to the same file reuses its DiffEditorViewModel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same computation ran eagerly before the editor became usable rather than on first visibility/navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Range reveal and next/previous-change positioning wait for the target diff; ordinary unrelated editor progress does not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unique files actually visited or expanded V, after virtualization and per-item coalescing; cost grows with V rather than total files N. Slowly traversing every file makes V=N.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Visibility-triggered work is bounded by the simultaneously rendered expanded viewport items, plus any explicit navigation target and the initial five. Each item's two sides are parallel; there is no shared global limiter, but this is materially smaller than the prior N-file startup burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold first access performs resolution and diffing. Warm repeat access uses the cached ObservableLazyPromise result. Failures are cached as loadError and are not retried per render. Loaded models intentionally remain until editor disposal; removed/in-flight items release resolved references after completion.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: template binding loads only uncollapsed rendered items, navigation calls the same lazy promise, and tests cover duplicate calls, collapsed files, slow targets, and superseded navigation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Viewport size, file-provider latency, and how quickly users traverse the list vary. The load cardinality and coalescing are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Boundary placement moves to first use, but absolute work is reduced to visited files and coalesced; the previous editor could not become usable until every boundary call completed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Save or revert a multi-diff containing loaded and unloaded files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action scans all N lightweight items, then awaits save/revert operations only for loaded modified models or dirty unloaded resources; it does not load missing text/diff models.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Save or revert eligible original/modified resources through ITextFileService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one modified call for each loaded item plus dirty unloaded modified items, and one original call only when dirty. Calls are issued with Promise.all.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every item was loaded before the action and the old path called save/revert for every modified model, plus dirty originals; changed behavior is equal or lower boundary cardinality for the same set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The save/revert command waits for all eligible filesystem operations, while clean unloaded resources incur only an in-memory dirty check.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total entries N for cheap dirty checks; expensive calls scale with loaded items L plus dirty unloaded items D, not all unloaded clean entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Eligible items and both sides are issued concurrently with Promise.all, as before. No new aggregate burst is introduced because the old implementation treated all N items as loaded and called every modified resource.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The action reads existing item/model state and dirty tracking; it neither triggers lazy loading nor changes the per-item model cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added test confirms a dirty unloaded resource is saved without additional model-reference requests, while loaded modified resources preserve prior behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously dirty files varies, but the changed call set is a subset of or equal to the old all-loaded behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The action avoids expensive model loading and reduces filesystem calls for clean unloaded entries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live change-set updates, item removal during loading, and editor disposal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resource metadata updates rebuild/reorder lightweight entries and may load newly visible or newly entering initial-five items. Removal/disposal does not wait for outstanding resolution, but completed references are released before they can create a diff model.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Finish any already-started text-model resolution for an item removed or disposed while loading, then release the resulting references.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the already-started original/modified pair for each concurrently removed loading item; stable keyed items retain and reuse their existing lazy state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old eager map could also leave in-flight resolutions that were disposed after completion, but it started them for every resource rather than only requested items.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion is off the UI update critical path; the item is removed immediately and no diff is computed after disposal.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number R of requested items removed while their model references are in flight; stable items are preserved by keyed observable mapping.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Only previously initiated loads continue. Disposal prevents subsequent synthetic-model creation/diff setup after each await check; there is no retry loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Stable items keep their loaded/failed promise across list updates. Removed items dispose their retained references; editor/widget disposal clears the view model and all loaded resources.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: disposal checks follow every asynchronous boundary and the test verifies both references are released with no additional diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rapid source churn can vary, but lifecycle behavior is directly tested for removal during a blocked load.
Scenarios.Verdict: No retention or cleanup regression found.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and all diff pages. Traced startup, viewport/navigation, save/revert, dynamic updates, disposal, model-resolution boundaries, worker diff computations, coalescing, caching, and concurrency. No actionable performance regression was introduced. Recorded the concrete eager-loading regression fixed by this PR and its blamed introducing commit.
